annotations.text:
Auracle operator console — direction: engineering instrument.
Dense, monospace for every identifier and number, light and dark on the theme tweak.

Three registers, one rule: monospace is what the ledger recorded, the sans is the console's own chrome, and a serif is words a person wrote or will read — at a reading measure, under 68 characters a line.

One rule the design enforces everywhere: the two gates are shown apart. No screen anywhere combines agreement and coverage into one confidence score.

The approve action is the one write on the whole console. It commits the same transaction as the command line. DEC-11 named it a rejected alternative, so it needed a register amendment before it shipped; DEC-40 is that amendment.

The reply is drawn because an approver who cannot read it cannot approve it. It is not editable here: the relay sends the helpdesk copy, so text typed on this console would be recorded and never sent.

A claim is drawn with the document it cites, and marked when the judge did not support it. Three states, never two: a claim nobody judged is not a claim the judge refused.

No rank and no score appears for a retrieved document. DEC-21 fuses ranks and keeps neither, so a column of scores would be a number the ledger does not hold.
